_note:
⛔ SNG-430. THE NAMING LAYER FOR MINTED FIGURES, WHICH NEVER EXISTED. `mintFigure` in worldtick.js says it outright: '⚠️ THE NAME IS AN EPITHET, NOT A NAME. The engine mints the slot and the story; NAMING IS AUTHORSHIP.' ⚠️ IT WAS RIGHT TO SAY SO AND NOTHING EVER CAME BACK TO DO THE AUTHORING. `worldtick.js` does not import `names.js` at all.
⛔ RESULT ON A LIVE SAVE: a figure named 'the one who outlived Cinder Vael, the Wright Who Would Not Stop', with `provisional: true` and `wants` holding 'of the the_ceaseless; watched Cinder Vael… called out, and outlived them'. FOUR FAULTS IN ONE RECORD — an epithet in the name slot, a double article ('the the_ceaseless'), a raw id shown to a player, and a SENTENCE FRAGMENT in the `wants` field.
_howToUse: ⚠️ On mint, draw a given name from the tradition pool and a byname from the origin pool, then set `provisional: false`. ⛔ THE EPITHET STAYS — as `epithet`, where it belongs. A figure is 'Sera Voight, who outlived the Wright' — not 'the one who outlived Cinder Vael, the Wright Who Would Not Stop'.
_wantsFix:
⛔ `wants` MUST BE A WANT, NOT AN ORIGIN. It currently holds the origin sentence, so a figure's stated desire reads 'of the the_ceaseless; watched X called out, and outlived them'. ⚠️ WANTS BY ORIGIN KIND:
   casualty_survivor → 'to be worth the one who did not come back'
   faction_leaderless → 'to be more than a stand-in'
   vacancy → 'to hold what nobody else would'
The ORIGIN belongs in `origin`, where it already is.

wants.casualty_survivor: to be worth the one who did not come back
wants.faction_leaderless: to be more than the one they settled for
wants.vacancy: to hold what nobody else would
wants._default: to be counted among those who matter

_displayFix: ⛔ 'of the the_ceaseless' — DOUBLE ARTICLE AND A RAW ID. `originOf` returns `home || people`, and homes are ids like `the_ceaseless`. ⚠️ THE ORIGIN LINE MUST RESOLVE THE ID TO A DISPLAY NAME AND NOT PREPEND 'the' TO A NAME THAT ALREADY HAS ONE. That is the same class as CCode's own note elsewhere in worldtick: 'NAMES, NOT IDS — dug in over arc_what_wakes_beneath is the machine talking'.

minted-1.was: the one who outlived Cinder Vael, the Wright Who Would Not Stop
minted-1._wasNote: ⛔ CCode, SNG-431. `minted-1` IS NOT A UNIQUE ID — it is the first figure minted in EVERY world, and applying this record by id alone overwrote a different player's figure (who outlived Saehara, not Cinder Vael) with this one's history. ⚠️ `was` is the identity check: the repair applies only to the figure it was actually written about. Everyone else keeps their own origin and is named from the pools instead.
minted-1.name: Sera Voight the Ashvow
minted-1.wants: to be worth the one who did not come back
minted-1.origin: of the Ceaseless; stood beside Cinder Vael when the Wright was called out, and outlived it
minted-1.why: ⛔ THIRD ATTEMPT, and the first two were both the wrong SHAPE. v1 'the one who outlived Cinder Vael' — a caption. v2 'Who Should Have Died First' — a subtitle, which Erik correctly rejected. ⚠️ v3 IS A NAME: Sera Voight the Ashvow. Two words after the name, no verb, no clause. She is a wright who survived a wright's death — so the byname is a VOW, which is what a survivor makes and what the valley calls her by. SHOUTABLE, and it still works when she reaches epic.

_standard:
⛔ ERIK: 'those are like SUBTITLES. I want names like Conan the Destroyer, Gandalf the White, Silas Weir the Necro-Wright, the Shadow Master, Pell the Iron Hammer.'
⚠️ HE IS DESCRIBING A DIFFERENT STRUCTURE AND I HAD THE WRONG ONE TWICE.
   MINE (v1): 'the one who outlived Cinder Vael' — an epithet, a caption.
   MINE (v2): 'Who Should Have Died First' — a SUBTITLE. It explains. It is a clause.
   ⛔ HIS: NAME + THE + SHORT NOUN PHRASE. Two or three words. NO VERB, NO 'WHO'.
     Gandalf the White · Pell the Iron Hammer · Silas Weir the Necro-Wright
⛔ THE TEST: CAN YOU SHOUT IT ACROSS A BATTLEFIELD? 'Sera Voight, Who Should Have Died First' cannot be shouted. 'Sera Voight the Ashvow' can.
⚠️ AND IT MUST BE BUILT FROM THE TRADITION'S OWN CRAFT-WORDS, which are authored and were sitting unused: Umbracraft, Palework, Radiance, the Edge, Ruinwork, Makecraft, Hourcraft, Falsecraft, Descent. That is where 'Necro-Wright' comes from in Erik's own example — CRAFT + ROLE, compounded.
_bynameNote:
⚠️ TITLE CASE, and WHO + PERFECT where the corpus uses it — these are how a world SPEAKS of someone, not how a log records them.
⛔ 'THE ONE THEY SENT INSTEAD' is the honest version of what I first wrote as 'who was not the first choice': same fact, but it is a thing a rival says with contempt and the bearer wears anyway, which is how a real byname works. 'WHO SHOULD HAVE DIED FIRST' is what a survivor is actually called, and what they think.
⚠️ A minted figure starts at `riffraff` or `notable` and CLIMBS. The byname must be worth carrying when they reach epic, because nobody renames a legend.
_originModifier:
⛔ THE ORIGIN SHARPENS THE BYNAME; IT DOES NOT BECOME IT. A survivor of an ashwarden's death is 'the Last Kindness' or 'the Ashvow' — the CRAFT names them, the DEATH chooses which. ⚠️ Prefer these from the tradition list when the origin fits:
   casualty_survivor → the darkest/most costly of the tradition's options
   faction_leaderless → the most FORMAL — they hold an office now
   vacancy → the most improvised
⛔ AND WHERE THE FIGURE IS OF A CRAFT THAT COMPOUNDS, COMPOUND IT. Erik's own example is the shape: 'Necro-Wright' = a dark thing + Makecraft. An umbral wright is 'the Shadow-Wright'; an ashwarden mason is 'the Cairnwright'. CRAFT + ROLE, one hyphen, no clause.
_repairNote: ⛔ SNG-431 §1. The staged registry repair from po/staged_content/name_repair_SNG-429.json, PROMOTED HERE so one file holds every authored name and one reader applies them. `repair` is keyed by MINTED FIGURE id (worldState.mintedFigures); `repairRegistry` by npcRegistry id. ⚠️ Both are applied ONCE per character, guarded by `nameRepairVersion` — a repair that re-runs would overwrite a name the player has since learned in play.

east-bank-stranger.name: Corrin Vale
east-bank-stranger.why: ⛔ WAS 'Unknown (east bank traveler)' — a description in a name field. ⚠️ Named from his own record: 'young and lean, patched wool coat, mud-caked boots — moves like someone who has walked a long way.' Vale for the country he crossed; Corrin is a road-name, short enough to be shouted.

third-farmer.name: Hessa Orm
third-farmer.why: ⛔ WAS 'Unknown farmer'. ⚠️ 'A quieter third party to the irrigation argument — has been staring at the ditch rather than at the people arguing.' Millbrook names run plain (Mara Wells, Dara Holt), so she is Hessa Orm: someone who watches the water instead of the quarrel.

cookhouse-boy.name: Tam
cookhouse-boy.why: ⛔ WAS 'Boy (name unknown)'. ⚠️ 'Maybe twelve, broom in hand — giving Silas the kind of attention children give to things adults refuse to look at.' ONE SYLLABLE AND NO SURNAME, deliberately: a cookhouse boy has a name people call across a room, and he has not earned a second one yet.
